name: A Day to Remember
label: Victory
lede: Five kids from Ocala, Florida played seven shows their first year, put a Kelly Clarkson cover and Ron Jeremy on Victory Records' dime, then sued the label, put out their own record mid-lawsuit, and walked away with a verdict.

eras.title: Seven shows in Ocala
eras.text: A Day to Remember came out of Ocala, a horse-country town in central Florida, mashing pop-punk choruses into metalcore breakdowns. The first year was barely a band; by 2005 they had a label and a debut album.

years.h: A Day to Remember forms in Ocala, Florida
years.p: Jeremy McKinnon sings, Neil Westfall and Tom Denney play guitar, Joshua Woodard bass and Bobby Scruggs drums. They play only seven shows in their first year.

years.h: Halos for Heros, Dirt for the Dead: the self-released EP
years.p: A Day to Remember's first release, followed in January 2005 by a six-song demo.

years.h: And Their Name Was Treason on Indianola Records
years.p: Signed to Indianola in February 2005, A Day to Remember's debut sells over 10,000 copies.

eras.title: Victory, Ron Jeremy and Kelly Clarkson
eras.text: Joshua Woodard's contact at Victory Records got the band to Chicago's biggest hardcore label. Their Victory debut came with a porn-star cameo and, on the reissue, a Kelly Clarkson cover that turned into a calling card.

years.h: A Day to Remember signs to Victory; Alex Shelnutt takes the drums
years.p: Bassist Joshua Woodard connected with a Victory representative; the signing was announced August 11. Alex Shelnutt replaces Bobby Scruggs this year.

years.h: For Those Who Have Heart, A Day to Remember's Victory debut
years.p: Recorded at Zing Studios in Westfield, Massachusetts, with Eric Arena. It reached No. 17 on Billboard's Heatseekers and sold 20,000 by September.
play: The Plot to Bomb the Panhandle

years.cap: A Day to Remember · via Discogs
years.h: Ron Jeremy turns up in The Plot to Bomb the Panhandle
years.p: The adult-film star makes a cameo in A Day to Remember's first Victory video.

years.cap: A Day to Remember · via Discogs
years.src: Wikipedia: For Those Who Have Heart
years.h: Victory reissues For Those Who Have Heart with Since U Been Gone
years.p: The reissue adds a [[Kelly Clarkson|d339efbb-77b9-4147-ba9e-59f2f24550b2]] cover and a DVD of a January 5, 2008 show at The Capitol in Ocala. It charts at No. 43 on Independent Albums; the cover's video follows in July.

years.h: Warped Tour 2008, writing Homesick on the road
years.p: A Day to Remember writes Homesick on Warped Tour 2008 and the Easycore Tour, then records it with [[New Found Glory|6acb932e-840d-47ac-8e0d-725ad8a6e52c]]'s Chad Gilbert producing. Kerrang! nominates them Best International Newcomer; Black Tide wins.

eras.title: Homesick and a Top 20
eras.text: Homesick made A Day to Remember the biggest new band on Victory, and What Separates Me from You went Top 20. One founding guitarist left to raise a family, and a replacement from Four Letter Lie stayed for good.

years.src: Wikipedia: Homesick (A Day to Remember album)
years.h: Homesick debuts at No. 21 and tops the indie chart
years.p: Recorded at The Wade Studio in Ocala with Chad Gilbert. It sold 22,000 in its first week and 200,000 by July 2010, and went gold in 2016.
years.xp:
Guests include Mike Hranica of [[The Devil Wears Prada|43c0958c-27ef-46c4-b4cc-83cfca54170d]], Vincent Bennett of [[The Acacia Strain|08bebce9-33fa-4ae9-9992-4e5d137d655b]] and Sierra Kusterbeck of VersaEmerge. Jeremy McKinnon said the closer If It Means a Lot to You took nearly a year to finish.

Have Faith in Me reached No. 40 on Billboard's Modern Rock chart in 2010.

years.h: Tom Denney leaves; Kevin Skaff joins A Day to Remember
years.p: Denney wanted to focus on his marriage, family and recording studio, and stayed involved in writing. Kevin Skaff, formerly of Four Letter Lie, becomes the permanent guitarist.

years.h: What Separates Me from You hits No. 11
years.p: Partly recorded, per the credits, on the back of a bus with no AC in Germany and in a closet in New Jersey. It sold 80,000 by December and went gold in 2016.

eras.title: Suing Victory, releasing it themselves
eras.text: The band said Victory owed it royalties; Victory said the band wanted out of a five-album deal for a major. While the case dragged on, A Day to Remember built a studio in Jeremy McKinnon's house and put out its own record.

years.h: National TV debut on Jimmy Kimmel Live!
years.p: A Day to Remember plays All I Want and Better Off This Way, then heads out on the Game Changers Tour with [[Bring Me the Horizon|074e3847-f67f-49f9-81f1-8c8cea147e8e]] in March.

years.big: $75,000 in royalties, or a five-album deal?
years.src: Wikipedia: A Day to Remember · Wikipedia: Common Courtesy
years.h: A Day to Remember goes public with its suit against Victory
years.p: The band, which had filed on May 31, 2011, said Victory owed it over $75,000 in royalties. Victory said the real issue was the band refusing to deliver five albums and wanting a major label.
years.xp:
The band then put out a statement saying it hadn't sought attention for the case and had no intention of speaking disparagingly about Victory.

Victory had been through a public split before: [[Thursday|0acae232-d31a-4211-b6d0-6af1b6350274]] left for Island in 2002 after its own fight with founder Tony Brummel.

years.h: An unmixed Violence (Enough Is Enough) leaks the new sound
years.p: Jeremy McKinnon said he wanted it dark and ominous, about things being out of your hands; some fans heard it as a lawsuit song.

years.h: Common Courtesy, self-released during the lawsuit
years.p: On October 4 a court let A Day to Remember release its own album while the case continued. Common Courtesy came out digitally four days later on ADTR Records; physical copies followed November 25.
years.xp:
It was made in a studio built in Jeremy McKinnon's Orlando home, later called Wade Studios, from early 2012 to March 2013. McKinnon and producer Andrew Wade put in $40,000 and the rest of the band $20,000. Chad Gilbert co-produced.

It sold 92,874 copies in its first week, reached No. 37 on the Billboard 200 and No. 1 on the UK Rock & Metal chart. The ruling still left the band owing Victory at least two more albums.

eras.title: Self Help and a verdict
eras.text: Jeremy McKinnon started his own festival, the band won Best Live Band, and in 2016 the Victory case finally went to verdict. Ocala handed them the keys to the city.

years.h: The first Self Help Fest, in San Bernardino
years.p: Jeremy McKinnon's festival debuts at the NOS Event Center with [[Bring Me the Horizon|074e3847-f67f-49f9-81f1-8c8cea147e8e]], [[Of Mice & Men|82b6784e-8161-42a0-9b5c-b9d31e63fd85]] and [[The Story So Far|bc303c9e-3ffb-49ca-acf1-088ef4d46ed7]]. It runs through 2017.

years.h: The Parks & Devastation Tour
years.p: A Day to Remember headlines with Bring Me the Horizon, [[Motionless in White|1c5b9bd6-76e8-4fe7-a6df-3bc0b5a452cc]] and [[Chiodos|b755836a-0cb6-4577-a678-55a5a6402d70]].

years.h: Alternative Press Music Awards: Best Live Band
years.p: A year after three nominations including Artist of the Year, A Day to Remember wins Best Live Band.

years.h: Bad Vibrations on Epitaph
years.p: A Day to Remember's first album on Epitaph Records, released while supporting [[Blink-182|0743b15a-3c32-48c8-ad58-cb325350befa]] on its July to October 2016 tour.

years.h: A Day to Remember wins its lawsuit against Victory
years.p: According to Wikipedia's Victory Records article, the band won three of the four issues and was given $4.02 million.

years.h: Ocala gives A Day to Remember the keys to the city
years.p: Presented at the band's homecoming show in Ocala.

eras.title: A founder out, a surprise album
eras.text: A Day to Remember moved to Fueled by Ramen and worked with Marshmello. Then its founding bassist left amid misconduct allegations and the revelation of a fatal 2017 crash, and the band later dropped an album with no warning.

years.h: Rescue Me with Marshmello
years.p: A Day to Remember's collaboration with the EDM producer [[Marshmello|301b45a4-b8b9-410e-8344-4b4eaf96691a]].

years.h: You're Welcome on Fueled by Ramen
years.p: A Day to Remember's seventh studio album.

years.h: Founding bassist Joshua Woodard leaves A Day to Remember
years.p: Per Wikipedia, he left over allegations of past sexual misconduct. It also emerged that in 2017 Woodard crossed three lanes of traffic in a crash that killed a 24-year-old driver.

years.h: Big Ole Album Vol. 1 arrives with no warning
years.p: A surprise self-release with singles Make It Make Sense and LeBron. It reached streaming services a month later, on March 21.
